topics.label: Lecture introduction and learning objectives
topics.groupedBecause: It introduces the lecturer, the scope of the lecture series, and the key learning outcomes regarding environmental carcinogenesis.

topics.label: Etiology of cancer: intrinsic factors, environmental exposures, and epidemiology
topics.groupedBecause: They examine the fundamental nature of cancer development, debating the relative contributions of endogenous cellular errors, genetic predisposition, and environmental exposures supported by epidemiological data.

topics.label: Pathogens and infectious agents in carcinogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: They explain how viral and bacterial infections contribute to malignant transformation, focusing on Burkitt lymphoma as an example of infectious oncogenesis.

topics.label: Mechanisms of chemical and physical mutagens
topics.groupedBecause: They detail the biochemical pathways and metabolic activation processes through which dietary toxins, UV radiation, cigarette smoke, and chemical pollutants damage DNA.

topics.label: Tumor promoters and multi-stage carcinogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: They explain the distinction between tumor initiators and promoters, showing how non-mutagenic agents drive chronic inflammation and cell proliferation.

topics.label: Host tissue susceptibility and summary of carcinogenic mechanisms
topics.groupedBecause: They examine how developmental timing and organ-specific factors modulate cancer risk, concluding with a comprehensive summary of carcinogenic mechanisms.

topics.label: Methodologies for identifying and proving carcinogenicity
topics.groupedBecause: They review the genomic, epidemiological, in vivo, and in vitro experimental approaches used to determine whether agents are carcinogenic.

topics.label: Summary and closing remarks
topics.groupedBecause: It concludes the lecture with a summary of environmental risks, carcinogenic potency evaluation, and personal risk-benefit decisions.
